references.text: The original command that Aaron and his sons should wash their hands and feet when entering the tent of meeting or approaching the altar, so that they would not die.
Describes the placement of the bronze basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and that Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet in it.
Moses was commanded to bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water as part of their consecration.
Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water, in obedience to the Lord's command.
The New Testament speaks of approaching God with a sincere heart and a body washed with pure water, fulfilling the picture of the Levitical cleansings.
Direct connection between the law's command to wash to avoid death and its actual fulfillment.
